Antigravity mercury propelling Spheres - China patent

#ufotwitter

China patent unlike that of United States patent uses different electromagnetic variation. It tries to create internal force using moving mercury + electromagnetic effects.

🧾 CN110857151A — what it actually proposes

According to the patent description:

-Uses rotating mercury (liquid metal) spheres
-Combined with:

Electric fields
Magnetic fields
High-speed rotation

Claims to generate “antigravity” or upward force

Key idea:

CN111038740A is a Chinese patent publication describing an “electromagnetic antigravity”–type propulsion device. It proposes using specially arranged electromagnetic fields and rotating working media (such as conductive fluids) to generate a force that counteracts gravity, with the ambition of enabling vehicles that can hover, maneuver freely, and potentially operate in space without conventional propellant.

Basic concept and structure

The patent belongs to the family of Chinese “antigravity” / EM-propulsion concepts where a closed structure—often a spherical or dish-like shell—contains an inner arrangement of conductors, capacitors and magnets. In related designs, a conductive fluid such as mercury circulates at high speed in a toroidal or spherical channel under electromagnetic forces.

The claimed mechanism is that the circulating medium, combined with strong magnetic fields, produces a resultant force on the enclosing structure whose net direction is opposite to local gravity, so the craft could hover or accelerate without reaction mass. In some embodiments, the power electronics and control systems sit in a central or lower “control cabin,” while the antigravity unit forms an upper “propulsion cabin.”

Claimed performance and applications

The text (and closely related Chinese antigravity patents) describes ambitious capabilities: free takeoff and landing, hovering, arbitrary-direction motion, operation in vacuum (no air needed for lift), low noise, and use of electrical power instead of chemical fuel. Proposed applications include transport vehicles, aerial work platforms, and even deep-space flight.

From the standpoint of contemporary physics, devices that locally cancel gravity via static electromagnetic fields contradict general relativity and well-tested principles like the equivalence principle.

Existing high-field EM experiments and precision gravimetry have not observed such antigravity effects. As with many “EM antigravity” patents worldwide, CN111038740A should be viewed as documenting an inventor’s concept rather than as evidence that practical antigravity propulsion exists.

This part from patent description is of utmost importance to us ordinary citizens:

"EM antigravity” patents should be viewed as documenting an inventor’s concept rather than as evidence that practical antigravity propulsion exists"

But somehow we see “concepts” of those patented UFO vehicles all over the world, underwater, in space, and in all different shapes and sizes, as if it isn't huge coincidence.
